support_jane: Customer ticket #C-12847 — streaming responses showing normal TTFB but large p99 total latency (10-20s). Non-streaming endpoints are fine. Repro steps and traces attached. Can someone take a look? :eyes:

matt_engineer: Understood. Do we have request IDs and whether they were h2 or http/1.1?

support_jane: req ids: rq_7a9c, rq_7b01, rq_7b2f. Most from EU region, client says using SSE over http/1.1 through a customer proxy (managed CDN).

sam_sre: Quick check: are streaming chunks being coalesced by intermediate proxies? That would make TTFB (first chunk) look fine but total long because later chunks are buffered then flushed. Any chunk timestamps in traces?

support_jane: I uploaded trace for rq_7a9c — shows first chunk at 120ms, then 95% of token stream arrives in a burst ~12s later. Attached: trace span ids + raw chunk arrival times.

matt_engineer: Paste of trace snippet: ```span:stream.write first_chunk=0.12s; chunk_2=12.2s; chunk_3=12.25s```

elaine_prod: Customer proxy is listed as CloudProxy v2 in ticket. That product is known to coalesce small writes on http/1.1 unless `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` flushes are explicit. Do we explicitly flush after each chunk?

matt_engineer: We flush at runtime boundary but rely on socket-level flush. If a proxy buffers, it can combine. We do include `content-type: text/event-stream` for SSE and use chunked encoding. But some proxies still buffer until a window or newline.

sam_sre: Repro plan: 1) attempt direct connection bypassing customer proxy (curl streaming to our edge). 2) reproduce with http/2 and http/1.1. 3) capture raw TCP to confirm interarrival.

support_jane: Customer provided a repro harness (small node script) that hits prod via their proxy. They can point to a staging endpoint for our tests.

matt_engineer: I ran the harness against staging via their proxy — confirmed same behavior: first chunk immediate, then huge pause, then giant flush. When I hit staging directly from my laptop (no proxy) it streams properly. So it's definitely being coalesced midstream.

ops_kate: Is this a regression? Any recent changes to how we buffer or how we do flushes?

matt_engineer: No code change in streaming flush logic last 30 days. We rolled a revised edge nginx config last week that touched proxy_buffering settings for HTTP/2 prioritization. Could be interacting badly with customer proxies.

sam_sre: Short mitigation options: 1) Suggest customer bypass or adjust their proxy config (disable response buffering for SSE endpoints). 2) Provide a non-streaming fallback endpoint until they patch. 3) Server-side: coalesce larger initial chunks (send periodic keepalive comments `:keepalive

`) to prevent proxy from idling — but that increases token cost and might break semantics.

matt_engineer: Quick experiment: I pushed a staging tweak to emit a 1KB padding comment every 500ms for 5s, then normal chunks. That avoided coalescing on customer proxy in my test. Not ideal long-term but could be a temporary workaround.

deploy-bot: deploy: matt_engineer pushed staging change (stream-padding) to staging at 2026-03-16T14:10:12Z — build #st-4021

support_jane: Customer willing to try a temporary safe patch if it avoids user impact. They want action plan to present to their ops.

elaine_prod: Proposed playbook for customer: 1) Short term: enable non-streaming fallback for critical endpoints OR accept our staging padding patch (we can expose as query param ?force_stream_padding=1). 2) Medium: customer disables buffering for SSE/streaming routes in their proxy (CloudProxy docs: set `BufferResponse false` for named route). 3) Long: we add documentation and a compatibility test in our onboarding checks to detect proxies that coalesce.

matt_engineer: I'll add a quick feature flag `x-stream-padding` header support so we can toggle padding per-request. That way we don't change global behavior.

sam_sre: Also adding an observability metric: chunk_interarrival_p50/p95/p99 per route and a tag for client-proxy (based on incoming Via header) so Support can quickly see when a proxy is coalescing.

ops_kate: Any risk of this padding breaking client parsers? Some SSE clients expect only event data. We should send as comment lines (`:pad <base64>
`) to be SSE-safe.

matt_engineer: Yep we'll use SSE comment `: ` prefix to stay SSE-compatible and tiny base64 blocks to avoid Unicode issues. Documented in PR.

deploy-bot: deploy: matt_engineer opened PR #4527 (stream-padding header + metrics). CI passed.

support_jane: Customer agreed to test staging with ?force_stream_padding=1 and report. I'll coordinate and update ticket.

elaine_prod: Follow-up: create KB doc for customers about proxy buffering + recommended proxy configs (CloudProxy, FastEdge, legacy-cdn). Also add automated onboarding check that simulates small-chunk stream and validates chunk interarrival at client side.

matt_engineer: Action items for me: (1) ship header toggle and pad implementation (PR linked), (2) add metric for chunk interarrival, (3) add docs snippet in support KB. ETA EOD tomorrow.

sam_sre: Action items for me: (1) add alert rule for chunk_interarrival_p99 > 5s for any high-traffic route, (2) create runbook for triage (how to confirm proxy coalescing).

support_jane: Thanks team. If padding works for their staging test, we'll recommend it as short-term fix and schedule a contact with the customer's proxy vendor for a permanent config change.

matt_engineer: One more thought — for critical customers we can also add an API-level fallback: if streaming p99 breaches threshold, auto-switch to a buffered response with an informative `X-Fallback-Reason` header so apps can degrade gracefully. Adding that to backlog.

ops_kate: Noted. Logging follow-up: add the customer's proxy fingerprint to their account metadata so future incidents are faster to diagnose.

support_jane: Last update: customer tested staging with padding header — confirmed p99 dropped from ~18s to ~0.8s for same workload. They've accepted short-term toggle. Moving to close after we ship metrics + KB. :white_check_mark:
